Two adult hands are visible, rhythmically touching the toddler's head and shoulders in time with a song. The lighting is bright and natural, coming from a nearby window. (2) The scene cuts slightly closer to the toddler's face as the hands move to her ears, eyes, mouth, and nose. She has a curious and slightly distracted expression, occasionally looking off-camera. A few toys and household items are visible in the soft-focus background. (3) The toddler is now sitting on a wooden floor in a more open area of the living room. Another young girl, slightly older and wearing a black t-shirt, stands nearby. The background reveals a clean, modern home interior with a sofa and cabinets. (4) The older girl begins to perform the dance moves, touching her head and shoulders, while the toddler watches or participates. A ginger cat enters the frame and walks across the floor in the background. The camera remains mostly static at a low angle. (5) An adult's hand points toward the toddler's head, and she responds by touching her hair and shoulders as prompted. She then leans forward to touch her toes. The final scene shows both girls together on the floor, laughing and making playful faces toward the camera. (6) The video concludes with a solid pink screen featuring a cartoon illustration of a young girl with pigtails and the text POPO'S DAILY LIFE in a clean white font.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a high-tempo, major-key melody on a synthesizer or bright piano, accompanied by a female child singing 'Head, shoulders, knees and toes.' The vocal is bright and rhythmic. (2) As the singing continues, a sharp percussive click triggers a transition. An adult male voice enters with high energy, saying 'Good, now your turn,' in Mandarin, overlaying the background music which drops slightly in volume. (3) The BGM restarts with the same bouncy tempo. The sound of light footsteps and fabric rustling is audible as the scene shifts. The female child's singing becomes more prominent again, with clear articulation. (4) A secondary child's voice can be heard laughing in the background. The adult male continues to provide vocal prompts like 'Where is the head?' with rising intonation, creating a call-and-response structure with the toddler. (5) The music reaches a crescendo and then stops abruptly with a soft chime sound. High-pitched joyful screaming and laughter from the children dominate the track, followed by a final short, sweet jingle that plays over the outro graphic.
